Subject: Demo recap + procurement checklist (procurement lane & MSA phasing)

Hi Claire / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time to run through the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone has alignment: 

What we covered
- Live demo of low-latency generation, quantization options, and RBAC controls.
- Previewed console cost and latency dashboards and canary rollout flow.
- Discussed Medicore's requirements: PHI adjacency, SOC2 evidence, procurement gating on MSA + DPA, and an exec-level SLA ask for steady-state latency.

Decision criteria you listed
- Security evidentiary artifacts (SOC2 report + data flow diagram)
- Procurement lead to own commercial terms and PO cadence
- Economic buyer sign-off for any multi-quarter reserved commitment

Immediate asks / proposed MOP
1) Confirm economic buyer and procurement owner (name + best email).
2) We'll send an editable MSA with redline guidance and a short DPA draft for parallel review.
3) Request security contact to kick off questionnaire (we can host an answers drive).
4) Sign NDA to enable sharing of customer-specific benchmarks (can be quick — we attached a simple NDA).

Suggested timeline (high level)
- NDA: immediate (1-3 business days)
- DPA + security questionnaire: parallel (3-7 business days for initial pass)
- MSA redline iteration: 5-10 business days depending on legal cadence
- Exec approval / procurement PO: target by 3/22 if reviews move on schedule

Attachments: Medicore_NDA_signed_20270311.pdf (we used your template to expedite), sample SOW outline.

If that looks right, can you confirm owners for: economic buyer, procurement lead, and infosec reviewer? Once we have that I’ll coordinate Karthik and our legal team for sequencing.

Thanks —

Evelyn Hart

Thanks Evelyn — good summary. Quick answers from our side: 

- Economic buyer: Tom Hsu (CTO) — tom.hsu@medicore.com. He will need a short business case showing cost delta vs our current vendor.
- Procurement lead: Sara Klein (cc’d). She owns contracting cadence and PO templates.
- Infosec contact: Rajiv Patel (cloud-security) — rajiv.patel@medicore.com. He asked to see our SOC2 plus a short SAML/SCIM diagram and our data retention controls.

On sequencing: we prefer NDA first (we’ve signed it as requested), then DPA + security review in parallel with MSA redline. Our legal typically pushes back on indemnity and data residency clauses — curious what your standard positions are and expected turn time once we share redlines.

Also can you share an editable MSA (Word) and a short one-page commercial summary Tom can review?

—Claire

Evelyn —

Thanks for the recap. Looping Marissa from Legal to own the contract thread. High-level legal sequencing recommendation based on Medicore’s asks: 

1) NDA (completed) — good to have it on file; we’ll store the signed copy.
2) Security evidence / questionnaire + DPA — run in parallel. Our privacy team can fill a DPA draft while Rajiv reviews the questionnaire; expect a first-pass DPA within 3 business days once we get answers.
3) MSA redline sequencing — recommended flow:
   - Redwood sends editable MSA (we’ll include redline guidance and our preferred alternative language for indemnity/data residency).
   - Medicore legal returns initial redlines (we typically see 1-2 rounds).
   - If indemnity/residency are high-friction, propose a short carveout appendix for PHI adjacency to keep timelines moving.

Estimated legal turn times (typical):
- Initial MSA send: same day (we can send today)
- First redline back: ~5 business days from receipt
- Resolution rounds: additional 3-5 business days depending on concessions

Deliverables we will produce for you:
- Editable MSA (Word) + a redline guidance doc
- DPA template tailored to EU/US residency language where needed
- SOC2 summary and data flow diagram for Rajiv
Marissa will own incoming redlines; please CC her on any legal responses so we have a single thread.
Attachments: Medicore_MSA_redline_20270314.docx (will be shared via secure Drive)
